title: Tech Note: Making Labels More Dynamic

historical_commentary.text: This note offers a simple, generic technique using flashing labels as a visual cue to draw a user's attention back to a field that failed an entry rule and needs re-entry, rather than only relying on a modal error dialog. The general UX goal — giving clear, in-context visual feedback for invalid form input — is timeless and still relevant, though the specific blinking-label implementation (likely built on classic timers/On Timer form events) would today more likely be implemented with modern styling cues (colored borders, inline messages, or tooltips) common in current UI conventions.
related_updates: Modern form UX generally favors inline validation messages, colored field borders, or icons over blinking text for drawing attention to invalid fields
The underlying 4D mechanism for timed/animated visual effects (form object property changes driven by a timer) is still available in current classic-language forms
